headline: Resilient despite higher oil, sticky inflation and higher-for-longer rates; institutional ETF demand buying every dip; increasingly behaving like gold rather than equities with further gains expected over the next year
reasoning: Milmeister argues Bitcoin is showing resilience against a tougher macro backdrop of higher oil prices, sticky inflation and higher-for-longer interest rate expectations. Institutional demand, including via ETFs and large investors, has supported prices with every dip attracting buyers. He believes Bitcoin is entering a new phase where it behaves more like gold than equities. He expects further price gains over the next year, with US and Australian regulatory developments providing additional catalysts.
quote: Bitcoin continues to show resilience despite higher oil prices, sticky inflation and expectations for higher-for-longer interest rates. Institutional demand, including ETFs and large investors, has supported the market, with every dip attracting buyers. Milmeister believes Bitcoin is entering a new phase and increasingly behaving like gold rather than equities. He expects further gains over the next year, while regulatory developments in the US and Australia could provide additional catalysts.
episode_title: Bitcoin defies tougher backdrop for risk assets

headline: Higher-for-longer rates are a headwind but institutional dip-buying is absorbing every selloff in crypto markets
reasoning: Michael Milmeister notes that the Fed's hawkish stance at Jackson Hole and rising oil prices are negative for risk assets including Bitcoin, but observes that every dip is being bought aggressively and quickly. He attributes this resilience to surging institutional demand visible in ETFs and through Stormrake's own order flow. He views this as a conducive environment for buying the dip despite the macro backdrop.
quote: As you mentioned, obviously Jackson Hole saw wash the new Fed chair be really hawkish and it looks like interest rates will stay higher for longer, which is not necessarily great for risk assets like Bitcoin. But what we've seen is every dip that's been caused has been brought up really, really quickly. And that's because there is a lot of institutional demand coming into the space. This is a perfect time to buy the dip, I guess.
episode_title: Why Bitcoin is defying the macro backdrop

headline: US Clarity Act delay is a background catalyst; passage would be another leg up for Bitcoin
reasoning: Milmeister notes market hopes have been pinned to the Clarity Act passing in the US, but it has been delayed and not yet finalised. He views eventual passage as an additional bullish catalyst for Bitcoin. In Australia, the incoming AFL licensing regime requiring crypto operators to apply for an AFSL by 30 September is expected to improve trust and the perception of the asset class in traditional markets.
quote: There's been a lot of hope in the market from the Clarity Act potentially being able to pass. Now that's been delayed and it has not yet finalised, but that is something that is in the background. And if that does happen, it's going to be another catalyst for Bitcoin to go higher. In Australia as well we're seeing the AFL regime come in and by the 30th of September, which is the end of this month, anyone that's in the crypto field in Bitcoin is going to have to apply for an air or so.
episode_title: Why Bitcoin is defying the macro backdrop

headline: Decoupling from the S&P, re-correlating with gold, and 30–40% upside to surpass total global dollar market cap within a year
reasoning: Milmeister argues Bitcoin is a superior store of monetary value and a defensive asset offering self-custody protection against government encroachment on savings. He highlights a recent 22% monthly gain for Bitcoin versus only 3% for the S&P, citing this divergence as evidence of structural decoupling. His 12-month price target implies a 30–40% rise from current levels to surpass the total market cap of all US dollars. Regulatory tailwinds — notably the US Clarity Act and Australia's AFL licensing regime — are additional potential catalysts.
quote: Fundamentally, I think Bitcoin is a far better system for monetary value. And it's also, you know, we're seeing a situation where many governments are looking at superannuation and how they can dip into it and that sort of thing. Now Bitcoin offers something that protects from that. You can hold it yourself. So it's a completely different asset type. So in terms of a defensive asset, it's really strong. It's now being correlated to gold a lot closer than the S&P. The S&P was very correlated to Bitcoin for a long period of time. And now we're seeing that decoupling. We're seeing BTC last month increased by 22% / 3% rise in the S&P. So we're seeing Bitcoin act differently in this market and that's really fantastic. Now in terms of my prediction, I think within a year we're going to see the market cap of Bitcoin be greater than the market cap of all dollars.
episode_title: Why Bitcoin is defying the macro backdrop
